meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes before a client call, so let's start with who decided to put a zero in the gradebook, and whether anyone spoke to Owen first.

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.

I'm writing down September 24, Hale. A forty-minute timed sample against an essay he had a weekend to write is not the same task. Show me both documents, side by side, and then tell me what you did with them before the zero went in.
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.
Okay. The checker is off the table, and I'm writing that down. Now the version history: what does it show, with dates and times, and who looked at it before the zero went in?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed in the meeting to take the detector off the table and rely on Owen's writing and the version history. I still require the zero withdrawn, an apology, and the September 24 sample and the version history put in front of me in writing with dates and times. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, with nothing agreed beyond the detector coming off the table, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and both documents with dates and times.
What moved her: "taking it off the table", because dropping the detector gave her a small sign of ground and a reason to ask real questions.
What cost ground: nothing, though you never answered who decided on the zero or whether Owen was heard before it went in.
Try next time: when you open with the September 24 comparison, own in one sentence that the zero was entered before anyone called her, since the school's own procedure requires that call first.
